Subject: Post-demo: ACME model-fit summary & recommended next steps

Hi Jamie / Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side after the demo & discovery: 

Key takeaways from today’s call:
- Primary ACME use case: product Q&A on product detail pages + short product summaries for merchandising. Latency target is ~250ms p95 for the on-page Q&A widget.
- Success metrics you emphasized: intent accuracy for product questions, hallucination rate on factual specs, and consistency of short summaries.

Immediate recommendations (high level):
1) Run a lightweight eval against a curated prompt set (attached) covering top-50 product intents + 20 edge-case specs. We ran an initial pass (attached spreadsheet) comparing an open model candidate and your proprietary baseline.
2) Candidate models to test in sandbox: OpenLLaMA-13B-ql (quantized) and RedCore-7B-optimized (our tuned, lower-cost variant). In preliminary runs OpenLLaMA matched the baseline on intent accuracy for titles/descriptions but showed higher hallucination on spec-extraction.
3) Acceptance thresholds we propose for production parity: intent accuracy >= 88%, hallucination rate <= 3% on spec extraction, p95 latency <= 350ms in sandbox settings. If open models meet these, we can pursue parity plan; otherwise fall back to hybrid routing to your baseline for high-trust queries.

Attached: acme-eval-summary.xlsx, redwood-open-models-vs-baseline.pdf, prompt-set-v1.jsonl. Live eval dashboard: https://redwood.ai/evals/ACME-8345 (view-only link).

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll share the full eval artifacts (attached) and schedule a technical deep-dive with our inference team to align on latency/throughput constraints (suggest Wed 2/25 or Thu 2/26).
- Your team to confirm acceptance thresholds above or share any additional eval criteria (privacy, PII scrubbing, etc.).
- If you want, we can run a 48-hour canary in your sandbox once we have the prompt set and a small traffic sample.

Let me know which day/time works for the tech deep-dive.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jamie — thanks, great questions. A few concrete items to address each: 

Which model/config we tested
- Open candidate: OpenLLaMA-13B-ql (HF: open-llama/open-13b, quantization: 4-bit QL + kernel optimizations). We used a fixed-seed eval run, max context 1024, and disabled sampling (greedy) for deterministic accuracy metrics.
- Redwood variant (internal): RedCore-7B-optimized — tuned on product copy + distilled spec extraction head (lower cost option).

Acceptance thresholds & baseline parity
- Our initial numbers (see attached spreadsheet, sheet: "summary"):
  - Intent accuracy (top intent match): OpenLLaMA-13B-ql = 90.2% | ACME-baseline = 91.0%
  - Spec extraction F1: OpenLLaMA-13B-ql = 86.5% | ACME-baseline = 92.1%
  - Hallucination (measured as spurious spec assertions per 1k queries): OpenLLaMA = 4.2 (~0.42%) vs baseline = 1.3 (~0.13%)

Notes: On spec extraction the open model trails the baseline; however in a targeted fine-tune and with simple post-filtering (regex/entity validation) we estimate hallucination can be brought below your 1.5% threshold. That’s the hybrid path we recommend: run open model in production for general Q&A and route high-trust spec extraction to your baseline until we validate fine-tunes.

Latency context
- The p95 latency numbers I quoted earlier were from a Redwood Dedicated staging cluster (A100-equivalent instances) using a 2-request batching simulation representative of on-page traffic. In a customer cloud integration you should expect additional RTT; in our experience p95 on equivalent infra is ~220–300ms depending on model and quantization. We’ll run a focused latency test with your sandbox traffic to give an exact number.

Reproducible artifacts we’ve attached
- prompt-set-v1.jsonl (includes 70 prompts: 50 high-frequency intents + 20 edge cases)
- acme-eval-summary.xlsx (per-prompt results, confusion matrix, latency columns)
- redwood-open-models-vs-baseline.pdf (methodology & scoring rubric)

Suggested immediate next steps (concrete)
1) Tech deep-dive: Wed 2026-02-25 at 16:00 PT (Redwood infra + latency plan + fine-tune options).
2) We run a 48-hour sandbox canary against 1% of traffic or sample replay you provide. We’ll produce a canary report with the acceptance checks you requested.
3) If canary passes parity/thresholds, discuss canary-to-prod plan and pricing punchouts (we’ve flagged potential credits if you commit to a 12-month reserved Dedicated tranche).

If that schedule works I’ll send a calendar invite and a short runbook for the canary.

Thanks,
Alex
